newsitem.title: USA: Phillips unit joins Daewoo, others in venture.
newsitem.headline: Phillips unit joins Daewoo, others in venture.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Wednesday its Canadian unit has joined Daewoo Corp of South Korea, Bechtel Enteprises of the U.S. and PAC-RIM LNG Inc of Calgary, in a US$1.0 billion liquefied natural gas project in western Canada.
Phillips Petroleum Canada Ltd holds a 35 percent participating interest in the project; Daewoo, 25 percent, PAC-RIM, 20 percent; and Bechtel, 10 percent.
South Korea's Korea Gas is expected to acquire the remaining 10 percent interest, it said.
Phillips said that one or more Canadian producers will also join the consortium as the project moves forward.

It said that under a memorandum of participation, the consortium members will build a facility that will produce 3.5 million metric tonnes of liquefied natural gas annually near Kitimat, British Columbia. It said the facility would be the largest LNG plant in North America and would be the third LNG plant to utilize Phillips' "optimized cascade" technology.
Construction is expected to begin later this year, with first deliveries to South Korea targeted for late 1999, it said.
Gas supply for the plant would be delivered through a proposed 24-inch pipeline from West Coast Energy which has a main trunk line at Summit Lake, British Columbia.
Production from the Kitimat plant will be exported to South Korea's Korea Gas.
"This project offers a new and expanding market opportunity for Canadian producers," said Ted Sandridge, Phillips' vice president of global ventures.

He said producers would have access to long-term stable pricing of gas and the opportunity to develop and produce gas previously shut in or stranded due to uncertain pricing and costly pipeline tariffs.
Activities surrounding the project, including meetings with gas supliers, negotiation of sales agreements, enviromental protection efforts and engineering studies, are well underway, he said.
Phillips, an integrated petroleum company, had revenues of US$15.8 billion in 1996.
